label: prop:electron-period-base
title: CAL-1 (m_e) is the n=0 base period of the prolongation tower
html:
Proposition. CAL-1 (m_e) is the n=0 base period of the prolongation tower

The prolonged Seiberg--Witten periods satisfy the one-parameter recurrence a_D^{(n+2)} = \tau\,a_D^{(n+1)} - a_D^{(n)} (prop:sl2-prolongation-recurrence). The n=0 term is the unprolonged period, the electron period a_D^{(e)} (prop:jet-sw-tau-decomposition). Identifying a_D^{(e)} with the leptonic scale m_e (CAL-1) establishes the first calibration as the base of the tower. Every period is generated from the triple (m_e,\,a_D^{(1)},\,\tau), and m_e propagates into every term through the recurrence rather than entering as an external multiplicative prefactor. Concretely, the n=2 period is a_D^{(2)} = \tau\,a_D^{(1)} - m_e.

The formal backing is QOU.Mass.second_period_contains_me, which derives that identity from the recurrence together with the base condition a_0 = m_e. The base condition itself is a defining field of the tower, not a result: it is the CAL-1 identification, and the accessor electron_period_is_base returns it verbatim.
